title: Property-driven Parallel Symbolic Model Checking of LTL
problem: Symbolic model checking for LTL properties faces state explosion challenge and lacks efficient parallelization of nested fixpoint calculations; most existing work focuses only on reachability or safety, not full LTL with fairness constraints.
motivation: Symbolic model checking has superior scalability over explicit methods, but parallelization of nested fixpoint computations required for full LTL verification remains largely unexplored.
method: The method creates a unified verification problem by combining the system being checked with a Büchi automaton (a mathematical machine for checking properties over infinite sequences) that represents the desired property. It then partitions the nested fixpoint calculations—the iterative verification process that finds the stable result satisfying the property—across this combined model-property structure and distributes them across multiple computers. A fairness-aware labeling function tracks states during this distributed computation, ensuring that infinite behaviors are treated impartially and that correctness under fairness constraints is maintained.
key_novelty: It is the first parallel symbolic model checking approach for full LTL properties, using fairness-aware state labeling to partition nested fixpoint calculations across the model-property product automaton.
contributions: Novel fair model state labeling function enabling partition of nested fixpoint across product automaton
Property-driven parallelization strategy for full LTL rather than just safety/reachability
Speedup ranging 2.81-17.19x on 32-core machine vs. sequential approach
33.1% average improvement over SOTA parallel BDD-based methods, 134% maximum

metrics.speedup: 2.81-17.19x on 32-core, average 33.1% vs SOTA BDD methods, up to 134% improvement
